solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: about means the bad-tempered word is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: grumpy means surly
prying, as in levering open, means prising

explanation.surface: Someone is unexpectedly bad-tempered about being snooped on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' looks like it qualifies 'grumpy', but it is the definition; 'prying' is used in the levering-open sense, and 'about' signals the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning in a way that causes astonishment or was not foreseen.

indicators.note: breaking down suggests something coming apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer collapses weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: John Stainer was a Victorian English church composer, known for The Crucifixion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Stainer is an example of an English composer, chiefly of church music.

indicators.note: either way means the letters read the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a gun reads the same both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' suggests a gun, but it means anything that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that turns or spins round an axis is a revolver in the literal sense.

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
a rim is an edge
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lists fabric, edging and carpet for a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpeting' means a telling-off here, not floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carpeted is British slang for receiving a formal rebuke from a superior.

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means the letters are sorted again

explanation.surface: Something is a final option for a man called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last resort' looks like a set phrase, but 'resort' is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack, as in Jack Tar, and salt are both old slang words for a sailor.

clue.text: Of limited height, secreting article — don't mention it!

indicators.note: secreting means hiding something inside

parts.note: something of limited height is not tall
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A short person hides something and asks that it not be mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are polite replies brushing off thanks, meaning it was no trouble.

clue.text: Most good fortune's to do with money

indicators.note: most means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: luck is good fortune
re means concerning or to do with

explanation.surface: A great fortune is all about money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, often viewed as gained dishonourably, as in filthy lucre.

parts.note: wally is British slang for a fool, as is jerk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fool wears a short coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a close-fitting, usually sleeveless jacket, a kind of short coat.

indicators.note: remixing suggests a re-arranged record, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A DJ is told to quit remixing a golden oldie.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is a command meaning wait or stop right there.

parts.note: auto is a short word for a motor car
a pilot drives or steers a vessel or aircraft

explanation.surface: A man named George is introduced as someone who drives a car.
explanation.walkthrough: George is old RAF slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot, so the name is the definition, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen's slang nicknamed the automatic flight-control system George, a crossword favourite.

indicators.note: in means the colour word sits inside the abbreviation for company

parts.note: cardinal is a shade of red, the colour of a cardinal's robes

explanation.surface: A churchman among company declares his faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests the prelate, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Credo is Latin for the phrase and names a statement of personal belief.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A teacher tells a fool to get on and memorise it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal insults for a foolish, stupid person.

parts.note: read literally, someone ran in an indecent way, that is naked, across a public place

explanation.surface: Someone hurried off unseemly fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indecent haste' is a stock phrase for unseemly speed; here the running is indecent because the runner is unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: To run naked through a public place, often at a sports event, is the verb's slang sense.

clue.text: Somewhat more readily go through the words again

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A reader goes over a text again a little more willingly.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a text a second time is to pass over its words once more.

indicators.note: retuning suggests altering, so the remaining letters are rearranged
almost means the word certainly loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is said to be out of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of 'certainly' to leave CERTAINL, which 'needs retuning' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind with a single reed is one example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Lacking first bit of Cheddar, game to go round for cheese

indicators.note: to go round means the shortened game surrounds the other piece
lacking means a letter is removed from the game

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game

indicators.note: first bit of means take the opening letter of the word Cheddar

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Without a bit of Cheddar, a game goes round for a cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking first bit of Cheddar' drops a C from the game, leaving ROQUET; 'to go round' then signals the wrap. Roquefort is a French blue cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A French blue cheese made from ewe's milk is one example of a cheese.

parts.note: depressed means down
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A gloomy team sees only the bad side of things.
explanation.definitionFit: The disadvantage or negative side of something is its downside.

clue.text: Secret feature at rear of house

definitions.meaning: a house's rear entrance, the opposite of the front one

explanation.definitionFit: A rear entrance gives its name to the sense of something done covertly or underhand.

clue.text: By containing irritation, could become spiteful

indicators.note: containing means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: taken as written
an itch is an irritation

explanation.surface: Holding in irritation might make someone mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Being malicious and snide in speech is a slang sense of spiteful.

parts.note: read literally, the first thing that rocks someone, a baby's rocking bed

explanation.surface: A pioneer of rock'n'roll music.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests a 1950s musician, but it is what rocks a baby early in life.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's rocking bed is the first thing to rock most people.

clue.text: Second question is hard, how to make squelching sound?

parts.note: taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone poses a second question about how hard it is to make a squelching noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To squash something soft so it squelches is the sense of this verb.

parts.note: someone from India is an Indian, a person of the East

explanation.surface: An Easterner takes over a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the states of the USA.

indicators.note: included means one word is put inside the other

parts.note: present means here
a bag is a sack

explanation.surface: A gift came with a sack of plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift but means here.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is herbaceous vegetation, plants collectively, especially grass for grazing.

clue.text: Saluting to a good man at home before midnight

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man
in means at home
the middle letter of the word night

explanation.surface: A man at home raises a glass just before midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is the centre of 'night', the letter G; 'before' just places it after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking a toast to someone is a way of honouring or saluting them.

indicators.note: found in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a tin is a can
an ox is a beef animal

explanation.surface: Poison is discovered in canned beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxin is a poison produced by a living organism.

clue.text: A handful run out with gold from salesman

parts.note: a hand has five fingers, and V is the Roman numeral five
to run out is to end
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A few people run out with gold taken from a salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of goods, especially from a stall, is a vendor.

clue.text: Stun for at least 48 hours, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken out loud

parts.note: 48 hours is two days, so the period lasts days

explanation.surface: Something knocks you out for two days or more.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze is to stun or stupefy someone, as with a blow.

clue.text: Part of ear makes one cross after endless suffering

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the shortened word
endless means the last letter is cut off the word for torment

parts.note: hell means great suffering
I is the Roman numeral one
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Constant pain in part of the ear makes someone irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims HELL to HEL; 'cross' looks like an adjective (angry) but is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved outer rim of the external ear is called by this anatomical name.

clue.text: Animator doodled a woman in love

indicators.note: doodled suggests idle scribbling, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cartoon animator sketched a lovestruck woman.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian-derived word names a female lover or sweetheart.

clue.text: Concern with judge's charge to borrower

parts.note: interest means concern, as in having a stake
to judge is to rate or assess

explanation.surface: A judge is worried about what a borrower must pay.
explanation.definitionFit: The percentage a lender charges on a loan is the cost to the borrower.
